editorial.headline: Electrical Networks, from Buildings to Public Infrastructure
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans the full life of electrical networks—and is nationally open to 100% foreign ownership without a Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Electrical network installation is a practical category, but its remit is deliberately wide. It covers the construction, installation, repair, maintenance and rebuilding of electrical networks in residential and non-residential buildings. Within that setting, the record expressly includes low-voltage networks, photovoltaic systems, power-storage systems and electric chargers. It reaches beyond buildings, too, to installation and maintenance of electrical networks in civil infrastructure such as highways, railways and airports. What unites the work is not the type of site but the electrical-network activity being carried out there.

The activity is available to enterprises at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. A business using it is describing the actual work it undertakes: electrical networks in buildings, the listed systems within them, or electrical networks associated with the stated civil settings. The scope encompasses a full cycle of work—building, installing, repairing, maintaining and rebuilding—rather than only a single moment of installation.

At national level, the foreign-investment position is direct. PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the record sets no national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. That is the national reading, and it should not be confused with Bali’s separate screening picture.

Bali is neither a copy of that national result nor a contradiction of it. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity is explicitly marked as not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the record adds a scale-specific point: at Large scale, OSS risk is Medium-High/High. There is no different Bali foreign-ownership percentage supplied here; the honest reading is simply that Bali does not impose the stated moratorium block on this activity, while the record identifies the Large-scale risk position. Nationally open at 100% and not moratorium-blocked in Bali is the precise headline—not a promise beyond the facts recorded.
